Maybe, but they would be bad games. Let me explain a moment. A good game with sufficiently engrossing narrative, story, and character depth such as to make me emotionally attached to a character, and then have that character or a significant other die, is going to fill me with a sense of regret and loss. This is a good thing, and although the effect may be momentarily stimulating the feeling will fade, and i will recognize that the game would be less impactful in the absence of the death/stimulating event.

There are however some games with poor stories that i wish they simply hadn't bothered to kill a particular character off in.

Good examples are games like "The Walking Dead" by Telltale Games, "The Dark Eye - Chains of Satanav", The Last of Us, and Final Fantasy 10.
